newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch June consumer prices rise 2.2 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Dutch June consumer prices rise 2.2 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The Dutch consumer price index (CPI) fell a provisional 0.5 percent in June from May, giving a 2.2 percent year-on-year rise, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
DUTCH CONSUMER PRICE INFLATION June 97 May 97 June 96
NOTES - Economists had expected the June CPI to rise between 2.3 percent and 2.5 percent year-on-year. EU-HARMONISED DUTCH INFLATION Monthly CPI pct change -0.5 +0.2 -0.5
The detailed non-harmonised index figures were:
108.8 Other goods, services 113 118.5 118.5 Consumer taxes, govt. services 37 153.7 153.7

The CBS said a drop in the consumer price index on a monthly basis was usual at this time of the year. It said notably prices of clothing, shoes and flowers had fallen in June, adding coffee, pork and patato prices had been on the rise.
Fresh vegetable prices fell over 12 percent in June compared to May, but on an annual basis prices rose over three percent.
The CBS said the drop in clothing and shoes prices, which was stronger than in June 1996, had been caused by the summer sales.
On a monthly basis, coffee prices rose some seven percent in June, while the rise on an annual basis amounted to over 20 percent, the CBS said.
Pork was almost two percent more expensive in June than in May, and cost some 13 percent more than in June of last year.
